blocking.item: Does ESPN populate prices? Is there a real-time channel?
blocking.note: Both halves answered. Prices yes; the draft room is SSE and REST stays empty — hence the CDP reader.
ffa strategy init — market-derived, editable; declared 2026-08-18

next.title: Calibrate the plan against your own four seasons
next.detail: The generated plan reserves $20 for the bench; the median team here spends $5 on its cheapest five picks, and 36 of 48 team-seasons spent $10 or less. That is ~$15 idle. The league's median WR spend is $92 against the plan's $78 — most of the gap is that reserve. Separately, max_on_one_player $70 is binding, not slack: the priciest player in four seasons went $80 and the top ten ranged $69-$80.
next.command:
# edit [strategy] in config/league.toml, then
ffa config check

next.title: Dashboard
next.detail: The largest remaining build, and it gates capabilities 6, 8 and 9. build_view() already emits every key the spec asks for, so it is front-end work against a frozen contract.

next.title: LLM layer
next.detail: Completes capability 2's intent half. Must sit beside the hot path, never inside it — advice is instant and cannot fail, and a network call in that loop would add latency and a failure mode while a clock runs.

next.title: Join the plan to nomination strategy
next.detail: nomination.py ships two candidate lists and deliberately no ranking, because ranking needed a strategy. There is now a strategy.

next.title: Post-draft grade (capability 11)
next.detail: Fires after the final pick, so it carries zero draft-day risk. The only item that can move past 08-31 without cost.

open_questions.q: What does the draft room's --selecting modifier mean while bidding is running?
open_questions.why: The seat that put this player up, or the seat due to put up the next one. Those are different teams, so nominated_by is deliberately left unwired rather than guessed — picking wrong would fire the stale-order banner on nearly every pick.
open_questions.how: tools/draft_watch.py already flashes it on change. One nomination landing in a rehearsal settles it.

open_questions.q: Does the real league's mDraftDetail backfill when the real draft completes?
open_questions.why: It would be a usable end-of-draft reconciliation pass. A practice draft can never answer it — ESPN reaps the ephemeral league the moment the draft ends.
open_questions.how: Only draft day can answer it. Nothing depends on it: the live path is the DOM either way.

open_questions.q: safe_legal_bid's optimistic ceiling has never fired live.
open_questions.why: No pick has yet arrived without a price, so `legal max` has never shown its `+`. Unit-tested and dry-run, but not seen in real traffic.
open_questions.how: Will exercise itself the first time ESPN sends a pick with no winning price.

notes.title: advise() cost
notes.body: ~40 ms at 100 sales, of which ~34 ms is nomination_plan scanning the remaining board. Fires once per user action, so it is invisible today. A surface that polls it many times a second is the case that would change that.
